text:
anya: quick sync re: onboarding pipeline tweaks — thinking about a cheap 'surface' pass that runs right after ingest to validate shape, tokenizer, and a tiny perf smoke. goal: detect obvious regressions in <5min.
raz: sounds useful. we had an incident where a new ckpt changed padding behavior and caused runtime token alignment issues. a quick alignment check would've caught it.
anya: exactly. proposed steps: (1) manifest validation (shapes, dtype, kv layout), (2) tokenizer mapping check (BOS/EOS/pad ids), (3) 200-sample microperf for short/long seqs, (4) basic logits diff vs a known golden for a seed set.
hugo: for logits diff, how strict? tiny model updates will naturally shift logits.
anya: set thresholds: token_mismatch -> immediate fail; shape/kv/manifest errors -> fail; logits drift > 0.15 JS divergence -> warn; p99 latency regression > 3x baseline or mem_peak > baseline*1.5 -> fail.
tera: enforcement depends on deployment tier. hosted dev keys: allow warn and auto-flag; dedicated/private: block for fail. we should encode this policy in registry as tier_policies.
raz: implementation detail: micropass should be a separate job, not inline in the ingest lambda. ingest should atomically register model and enqueue micropass. avoids backpressure.
anya: agreed. queue item fields: model_id, version, org, priority, requested_by, sample_set_id. runner picks up and writes micropass.status and micropass.report_url into registry metadata.
hugo: we need a lightweight report format: csv or small json. ops prefers no nested objects in metadata (keep strings). so metadata keys should be strings or lists of strings. brainstormed keys: micropass.status, micropass.metrics, micropass.artifacts=[report_url, golden_url]. store metrics as comma-separated string like "p50:12.3,p95:42.2,mem:2.1GB,js_div:0.08".
tera: good, makes registry queries simpler. also add micropass.run_ts and micropass.runner.
anya: rollout plan: enqueue models for micropass on ingest; if micropass.fail and tier=dedicated -> block admission and notify SEs; if warn -> auto-tag and create ticket in onboarding queue.
raz: what about cost? micropass should default to CPU instance unless model requires GPU to load — we can detect quantized vs fp16. fallback: try CPU first, if OOM then schedule GPU.
hugo: plus rate limits per org: default 5 concurrent micropasses; allow overrides for enterprise with dedicated capacity.
anya: edge case: some community models download large extra files at runtime. micropass runner should run inside network-sandboxed env and enforce 30s download timeout. if downloads exceed limit -> fail and mark reason.
tera: add monitoring: count micropass.per_org_queue_depth, micropass.latency_hist, and micropass.failure_reasons. send daily digest to onboarding SREs.
anya: I'll draft an RFC with schema snippets and sample CLI:
```
redwood-micropass run --model $MID --samples 200 --seedset small_dialogue --fast
```
output is a small json uploaded to GCS. registry metadata example: micropass.status=warn, micropass.metrics="p50:11.5,p95:34.2,mem:1.9GB,js:0.07", micropass.artifacts=["gs://bench-reports/123.json"], micropass.run_ts=1795567890
raz: lgtm. please include migration for older models: run micropass on models that exceed 10k requests/day within next 14d.
hugo: also add a human override flag for SEs: allow_skip_micropass=true recorded in audit logs when used.
onboard-bot: micropass queue created. docs: https://internal.redwood/onboard/micropass
anya: thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC and link the PR for the harness change. :memo:
